extracted.intended_audience: referees/reviewers for The EMBO Journal (scientists asked to peer-review manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for scientists acting as referees for manuscripts submitted to The EMBO Journal, covering confidentiality, conflicts of interest, review quality, anonymity, consulting colleagues, timelines, and cross-referee commentary. Intended to guide conduct and content of reviewer reports within EMBO Press's transparent-review model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should treat the review process as being strictly confidential, and manuscripts refereed for The EMBO Journal should not be discussed with anyone not directly involved in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts must not be shared or discussed with anyone not directly involved in the review. Maintain strict confidentiality of the manuscript content and review deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a conflict of interest regarding the manuscript you have been asked to review (e.g., it competes with your own work), you should immediately delete the manuscript file and decline to referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of conflicts include direct competition with your own work. If a conflict exists, do not proceed—delete local copies and inform the editor that you must decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Factually incorrect statements should be avoided, and arguments in favour or disfavour of a given study should be justified. Reviewers are encouraged to be very clear about what revision will be required for a manuscript to become acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid factual errors; support critiques and endorsements with justification. Clearly state the specific revisions or conditions under which the manuscript would be acceptable (e.g., experiments, analyses, clarifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should, as a rule, not disclose their identities to the authors or to other colleagues since they may be asked to comment on the criticisms of other referees and may then find it difficult to be objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reveal your identity to authors or colleagues. Anonymity protects objectivity, particularly when cross-referee commentary or later editorial discussion may require impartial assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting Colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: If colleagues are consulted, they should be identified to the editors. If experts from outside the referee's own laboratory are consulted, referees should check with the editors beforehand to avoid involving anyone who may have been excluded by the editor or the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking input from others, always inform and identify them to the editor. For external experts, obtain editorial approval first to ensure there are no exclusions or undisclosed conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent Peer Review Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press publishes the reviewer reports alongside published papers and maintains reviewer anonymity. Reviewers should note that their reports as well as the authors' point-by-point responses will be included in this transparent process document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that your report (with reviewer anonymity preserved) and the authors' responses will be publicly available with the published paper. Write reports accordingly—professional, factual, and clear—since they will be part of the published record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press asks that reviewers respond promptly or inform the journal if they anticipate a significant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot meet the requested deadline, notify the journal immediately. Prompt responses facilitate timely editorial decisions and reduce burden on authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Referee Commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press uses a model where reviewers can comment on each others' reviews after submission, which improves consistency and helps editors make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submitting your review you may have the opportunity to read and comment on other referees' reports; engage constructively to improve consistency and assist editorial judgment.
